span.label: The spread of computer viruses on the Internet, treated as an epidemic process running on a scale-free network.

span.label: Why do computer viruses persist for years at very low prevalence, when standard epidemic models say an infection either dies out exponentially or takes off?

span.label: Shows that on a scale-free network the epidemic threshold vanishes, so an infection persists at any spreading rate - which explains the observed long-lived, low-prevalence computer viruses without tuning anything.

span.label: Euclidean lattice → epidemic threshold
span.note: A NONZERO EPIDEMIC THRESHOLD IS A PROPERTY OF THE LOCAL-CONNECTIVITY REGIME, NOT SOMETHING THE LATTICE PRODUCES. The lattice does not increase, reduce or eliminate a threshold; models with local connectivity simply HAVE one, and that is the standard result this paper is written against. None of the eight types says `X holds in regime Y`, and none of the four effect directions says a quantity EXISTS - all four describe a change in it.
